name: Skeleton Recall Loss (skelRec)
what: Connectivity-conserving loss that scores the recall of the mask skeleton against the GT skeleton, computed with cheap CPU-side skeletonization (skimage) instead of differentiable GPU ops; first multi-class-capable topology loss for thin structures (Kirchhoff et al., ECCV 2024).
why_better: Old plan's soft-clDice needs differentiable morphological ops on the probability volume every step; skelRec replaces that with hard skeletonization on thresholded masks + straight-through gradients, so it runs ~10x cheaper in training time/memory while matching or beating clDice connectivity, which directly serves the neurite length/recall target and leaves GPU budget for the Swin multi-task heads.
evidence: 5 public tubular datasets (vessels/nerves/roads/cracks): 'overall superior performance to current state-of-the-art approaches ... substantially reducing computational overheads by more than 90%' (no single aggregate number in abstract).
source_title: Skeleton Recall Loss for Connectivity Conserving and Resource Efficient Segmentation of Thin Tubular Structures
fit_small_data: high - drop-in loss change on an existing U-Net/UNet++ backbone, no extra parameters or data
fit_onnx_cpu: high - the loss itself is training-only; inference model is unchanged and stays ONNX-exportable (skeletonization is CPU numpy anyway)
risk: A 2025 critical analysis (see separate item) found skelRec did not beat traditional baselines on several tubular datasets; must A/B against plain Dice+clDice on our own val set before committing

name: Critical evaluation of Skeleton-Recall Loss (Arora et al. 2025)
what: Theoretical gradient analysis plus empirical re-benchmark showing that topological skeleton-based losses, including the 2024 skelRec, often fail to exceed traditional Dice/CE baselines on tubular segmentation benchmarks.
why_better: Beats the old plan's implicit assumption that adding clDice-family losses is free upside: it gives a cheap pre-registered A/B protocol and a gradient explanation for when skeleton losses wash out (thin 2-3px structures produce tiny skeletons where the loss signal vanishes), preventing wasted weeks on a loss that may not move our length MAE <= 5um target.
evidence: Re-evaluated on the original SRL tubular datasets plus additional datasets: 'the performance of SRL-based segmentation models did not exceed traditional baseline models' (per-dataset numbers not in abstract).
source_title: Does the Skeleton-Recall Loss Really Work?
fit_small_data: high - it is an evaluation/analysis method, zero code dependency
risk: Their negative result may not transfer to 2D phase-contrast neurites (their benchmarks include 3D and large vessels); treat as hypothesis to falsify on our data, not as verdict

name: cbDice (Centerline Boundary Dice)
what: Boundary-aware extension of clDice (MICCAI 2024) that adds a mask-distance term and radius information from the vascular skeleton, so the loss penalizes broken branches and diameter errors in a balanced way instead of favoring thick vessels.
why_better: Old plan's soft-clDice is translation-insensitive (a shifted neurite with identical overlap scores the same) and diameter-biased; cbDice's boundary term + radius weighting makes it sensitive to exactly the errors that corrupt our 4 NTI parameters (broken branch = wrong branch count and length), at similar computational cost to clDice.
evidence: Validated on three vascular datasets (2D/3D, binary/multi-class); 'outstanding performance on the MICCAI 2023 TopCoW Challenge dataset' (no single number in abstract).
source_title: Centerline Boundary Dice Loss for Vascular Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - loss-only change, works on any U-Net/UNet++ with 70 images
fit_onnx_cpu: high - training-only loss; inference model unchanged for ONNX export
risk: Radius-from-skeleton term tuned for vessels of varying diameter; our neurites are uniform 2-3px, so the diameter-balance benefit may be marginal - A/B vs soft-clDice required

name: clCE (Centerline Cross-Entropy Loss)
what: MICCAI 2024 loss that applies cross-entropy on the centerline/skeleton pixels rather than full masks, claiming better topology consistency than Dice-class losses without sacrificing segmentation accuracy.
why_better: The old plan's CE+Dice+clDice stack is heavy and redundant; clCE targets the same thin-tube connectivity with a standard CE implementation (no differentiable skeleton needed), simplifying the multi-task loss to a 2-term sum and reducing hyperparameter coupling that currently makes 5-seed training fragile.
evidence: Vessel-like structures (coronary/vascular data): title claims 'Better Topology Consistency Without Sacrificing Accuracy'; specific numbers not in the abstract I could see (paywalled LNCS).
source_title: The Centerline-Cross Entropy Loss for Vessel-Like Structure Segmentation: Better Topology Consistency Without Sacrificing Accuracy
fit_small_data: high - trivial loss implementation, no data cost
risk: No official code found and full paper paywalled; implementation from description alone may differ from authors' (unverified details)

name: Efficient Betti Matching (C++ implementation, 3D-capable)
what: Highly optimized C++/Python implementation of the Betti-matching loss (induced matching of persistence barcodes, differentiable), with speedups over Cubical Ripser, making topology-aware training feasible instead of the prohibitively slow original.
why_better: Old plan listed 'basic TopoLoss/Betti matching' as known but never made it usable; this is the component that actually makes a Betti-matching term affordable inside a 15-week training loop, and it gives us the interpretable Betti-matching error metric for evaluation (more sensitive than plain Betti-number error) to quantify neurite connectivity quality in the NTI paper.
evidence: Improved topological correctness across several 3D segmentation datasets; 'significant speedups compared to Cubical Ripser' (per-dataset numbers not in abstract).
source_title: Efficient Betti Matching Enables Topology-Aware 3D Segmentation via Persistent Homology
fit_small_data: medium - loss is data-agnostic and cheap per image, but 2D masks via a 3D pipeline adds integration overhead; use only if the 2D Betti-matching repo lacks pieces we need
fit_onnx_cpu: high - training/evaluation only, C++ op is CPU-friendly; inference model untouched
risk: Overkill for 2D microscopy if the 2D Betti-matching repo suffices; Python/C++ interface integration could eat the 2-week budget

name: Topologically faithful multi-class segmentation (Betti matching for N classes)
what: MICCAI 2024 loss extending Betti matching to multi-class segmentation by projecting N classes to N single-class PH problems, validated on cardiac, cell, artery-vein and Circle of Willis data.
why_better: Our model is multi-task (soma instance + neurite semantic); the old plan's clDice only handles binary neurite masks, while this gives a principled topology term that works per-class (soma vs neurite) in one framework, directly improving the soma/neurite separation that feeds the morphology parameters.
evidence: Four medical datasets (cardiac, cell, artery-vein, CoW): 'significantly enhances topological correctness' while preserving volumetric performance (no per-dataset numbers in abstract).
source_title: Topologically Faithful Multi-class Segmentation in Medical Images
fit_small_data: high - loss change only; validated on datasets far smaller than 70-image-per-class scale
risk: Same persistent-homology cost concern as item 5; if per-iteration time is too high, combine with their per-class projection to keep it tractable

name: Topograph (graph-based strictly topology-preserving loss)
what: Graph-based framework that builds a component graph encoding prediction/label topology, identifies topologically critical regions, and aggregates a neighborhood loss with a strict homotopy-equivalence metric; proven topological guarantees and up to 5x faster loss than persistent-homology methods (2024, NeurIPS-era preprint).
why_better: Old plan's 'post-hoc bio prior vs NETMORPH' checks topology after the fact; Topograph enforces it during training with a formal guarantee (homotopy of union/intersection), at 5x lower cost than Betti matching, and its strict topological metric can serve as our Neurite Topology Score in the NTI validation instead of an ad-hoc NETMORPH comparison.
evidence: Binary and multi-class medical datasets: SOTA topological performance with 'up to fivefold faster loss computation compared to persistent homology methods' (per-dataset numbers not in abstract).
source_title: Topograph: An efficient Graph-Based Framework for Strictly Topology Preserving Image Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - loss-only, officially implemented, no data requirement
fit_onnx_cpu: high - training-only; pure graph ops on small 2D masks are cheap on CPU
risk: Loss operates on thresholded components; very thin (1px) skeleton-like neurites can produce spurious components that the metric penalizes hard - needs threshold/scale tuning

name: SDF-TopoNet (SDF pre-training + topology-aware fine-tuning)
what: Two-stage framework for tubular segmentation: pre-train on signed-distance-function targets (encoding topology implicitly and cheaply), then fine-tune with a dynamic adapter plus a refined topological loss to fix overfitting and cost issues of pure-PH losses.
why_better: The SDF head is a plain convolutional output - cheap to train on 70 images and a natural second head in our multi-task Swin model (soma + neurite + SDF) that yields both a distance-regularized neurite boundary (better length estimate) and a soft centerline for graph extraction, replacing the brittle post-hoc skeletonization in the old plan.
evidence: Five benchmark tubular datasets: outperforms existing methods 'in both topological accuracy and quantitative segmentation metrics, while significantly reducing training complexity' (no per-dataset numbers in abstract).
source_title: SDF-TopoNet: A Two-Stage Framework for Tubular Structure Segmentation via SDF Pre-training and Topology-Aware Fine-Tuning
fit_small_data: medium - SDF self-targets can be computed from 70 masks; two-stage training on this small set risks overfitting the fine-tune stage, needs early stopping
fit_onnx_cpu: high - SDF head is one extra convolution, fully ONNX-exportable; adds ~5-10% inference FLOPs
risk: Repo is a 1-star thesis codebase with no license; the 'dynamic adapter' detail is unverified and may not match our backbone

name: GATS (Geometric Assessment-driven Topological Smoothing)
what: Loss for 3D axon segmentation/centerline detection that replaces fixed-threshold morphological thinning with radius-aware geometric assessment plus average-pooling smoothing, formulated as a GATS loss (2023).
why_better: It is the only topology loss I found validated specifically on axons (the closest analog to cultured neurites), and its radius-assessment component solves the over-thinning problem that makes standard skeletonization unreliable on 2-3px neurites - directly supporting the length MAE <= 5um target where over-thinning creates spurious branches.
evidence: Multiple axon datasets: segmentation/centerline metrics up 2-5%, Betti error rates improved by 9% (abstract-stated).
source_title: Improved Topological Preservation in 3D Axon Segmentation and Centerline Detection using Geometric Assessment-driven Topological Smoothing (GATS)
fit_small_data: medium - designed for 3D volumes; adapting the radius-assessment to 2D phase-contrast requires re-deriving the scale space
fit_onnx_cpu: high - training-only loss; no inference component
risk: No code found; 2D adaptation of the 3D geometric assessment is non-trivial and unverified for brightfield/phase-contrast contrast

name: Topology-aware skeleton loss + DINOv3-initialized 3D neuron segmentation (NeurINO)
what: CVPR 2026 framework that adds an explicit topology-aware skeleton loss enforcing graph-based arbor fidelity, and initializes a 3D segmentation model from inflated 2D DINOv3 self-supervised weights for data-efficient neuron reconstruction.
why_better: Two transferable ideas beat the old plan: (1) the topology-aware skeleton loss is a ready recipe for our 'skeleton' task head (the old plan had a skeleton output but no topology term on it); (2) the inflation-based 2D->3D SSL initialization shows how to get morphology priors from a pretrained vision model without training one, a data-efficiency lever we have (70 labels) but the old plan did not exploit beyond Cellpose pre-annotation.
evidence: Four neuronal datasets (2x BigNeuron, NeuroFly, CWMBS): avg gains of 2.9% Entire-Structure Average, 2.8% Different-Structure Average, 3.8% Percentage of Different Structure over SoTA (abstract-stated).
source_title: NeuroSeg Meets DINOv3: Transferring 2D Self-Supervised Visual Priors to 3D Neuron Segmentation via DINOv3 Initialization
fit_small_data: medium - the skeleton-loss idea transfers to 2D; the DINOv3-inflation part is for 3D volumes and would need redesign for our 2D phase-contrast images (DINOv2/v3 zero-shot on light microscopy is separately known to work)
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - the skeleton head adds graph ops that need ONNX export verification; DINOv2/v3 features are feasible on CPU but slow if run per-inference (precompute instead)
risk: Paper is 2026 and 3D-centric; unverified whether the skeleton loss component is released separately from the full pipeline

name: VOF-Net (Vessel Oriented Filtering Network)
what: Embeds a learned vessel-orientation field into segmentation: an orientation-estimation network predicts local directions, and oriented filters convolved along those directions feed a segmentation net, encoding the prior that vessels are slender curved tubes (2022, CTA/MRA).
why_better: Old plan uses plain U-Net/DeepLabV3 convs that have no directional prior for 2-3px tubes; VOF-Net's oriented-filter bank acts as a learned vesselness-guided head that enhances exactly the thin elongated responses neurites produce, improving recall of faint neurite segments before the topology losses even act - a complementary gain rather than a competing loss.
evidence: CTA and MRA cerebrovascular datasets: 'embedding the specific vascular filter improves the segmentation performance' (no single number in abstract).
source_title: Cerebrovascular Segmentation via Vessel Oriented Filtering Network
fit_small_data: medium - adds an orientation head (a few conv layers); 70 images may be enough for a 2D version but needs validation
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - oriented filtering is convolutional and ONNX-friendly, but the two-stage orientation-then-segmentation pipeline doubles inference latency on CPU; can be fused or precomputed
risk: No code found; orientation field on 2-3px wide tubes is noisy at this scale (sub-pixel orientation), benefit unverified for phase-contrast cell imaging vs angiography

name: Vesselness-filter-fused U-Net inputs (ISBI 2024)
what: Trains an identical U-Net on Frangi-vesselness-filtered hyper-volumes instead of raw CT and shows improved segmentation of the same images, with gains concentrated on small vessels (2024).
why_better: Zero-architecture change: feeding a Frangi/ridge-filter channel (or its multi-scale variant) alongside raw phase-contrast is a 1-day experiment that specifically targets small-vessel/small-neurite recall - the failure mode behind our length-MAE miss - and it composes with any of the topology losses above (it is an input-channel trick, not a competing method).
evidence: Two vascular CT datasets: 'improved segmentations, especially for small vessels' when training on vesselness hyper-volumes vs raw images (no single number in abstract).
source_title: Deep vessel segmentation based on a new combination of vesselness filters
fit_small_data: high - preprocessing only; no extra parameters, works on 70 images
fit_onnx_cpu: high - filter can be precomputed offline and stored as an extra input channel; ONNX graph unchanged
risk: Frangi filter parameters (scales/beta/alpha) must be tuned to 2-3px neurite width; wrong scale range suppresses instead of enhances

name: ESRVS (Extreme Semi-Supervised Vessel Segmentation with one annotated image + DINOv3 features)
what: PRCV 2026 method for retinal vessel segmentation from a single annotated image plus an unlabeled pool: DINOv3 target-domain-adapted features build a multi-granular vessel prototype, pseudo-labels are generated and refined with weighted training and adversarial refinement.
why_better: The old plan's pseudo-label self-training uses its own model's confidence; ESRVS shows that transferring cues from a foundation model (DINOv3) with only 1-10% labels retains 93.7% of fully supervised Dice and 95.1% of clDice - for a project whose binding constraint is ~70 labels plus an unlabelled pool, this is the highest-leverage data-efficiency item in this list.
evidence: Eight public retinal vessel datasets: best Dice and clDice on 6/8 datasets and best HD95 on all 8 vs methods using 10-20% labeled data; Mask2Former retains 93.7% fully-supervised Dice, 95.1% clDice (abstract-stated).
source_title: ESRVS: Extreme Semi-Supervised Retinal Vessel Segmentation with a Single Annotated Image
fit_small_data: high - this is the extreme-small-label regime; 70 labelled + unlabelled pool is exactly its operating point
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - DINOv3 feature extraction is CPU-heavy per image but can be run once offline to cache features; the segmentation student itself is a normal U-Net/Transformer exportable to ONNX
risk: Domain gap: DINOv3 features are tuned for retinal fundus in the paper; phase-contrast cultured cells may need the target-domain adaptation step redone, and the gain may shrink (unverified)
